content: When mounting equipment on a foundation or coaming, the foundation or coaming must be elevated at least 4 inches (10.2 cm) above the finished deck. 3. Equipment must be sealed to the foundation or coaming using cement or a continuous weld. 4. For equipment not mounted on legs, a sealed-type foundation or coaming must be provided. 5. The overhang of equipment from the foundation or coaming must not exceed 4 inches (10.2 cm). 6. Any overhang of equipment along the bottom must be completely sealed. 7. Table-mounted equipment, unless easily movable, must either be sealed to the tabletop or mounted on legs at least 4 inches (10.2 cm) above the tabletop. 8. The backsplash attachment to the bulkhead must be continuous or tack-welded, polished, and sealed tightly. 9. Continuous welds must be used for attaching all food contact surfaces or connections from food contact surfaces to adjacent splash zones, ensuring seamless coved corners. 10. Only continuous polished welds are permitted for food contact surfaces and splash zones adjacent to food contact surfaces. 11. Splash zone attachments to the bulkhead, decking, or other equipment must be continuous or tack-welded, polished, and sealed tightly. 12. All gaps must be less than 1/32 inch (0.8 mm) before being sealed. 13. If fasteners are used, they must be low-profile, non-slotted, and non-corroding, ensuring the resulting gap is less than 1/32 inch (0.8 mm). 14. Bulkheads, deckheads, or decks receiving such attachments must be reinforced. 15. Gaps or seams must not be left, and exposed slotted screws, Phillips head screws, or pop rivets must not be used in food splash zones or on food contact surfaces. 16. For non-food contact surfaces of equipment, gaps and seams must not exceed 1/32 inch (0.8 mm). 17. Gaps less than 3/32 inch (3.2 mm) must be sealed with an approved sealant. 18. For surfaces exposed to extreme temperatures or gaps greater than 3/32 inch (3.2 mm), stainless steel profile strips must be used. 19. Pop rivets, Phillips head screws, slotted screws, and other fasteners used in non-food contact areas must be made of corrosion-resistant materials. 20. Built-in equipment hinges and latches must be durable, non-corroding, and easily cleanable. 21. Equipment gaskets for reach-in refrigerators, steamers, ice bins, and ice cream freezers must be made of smooth, non-absorbent, non-porous materials. 22. Gaskets must be closed and sealed at their ends and corners, and hollow sections must be sealed. 23. Refrigerator gaskets must be designed to be removable. 24. Fasteners used to install gaskets must conform to the requirements specified in Section VI. 25. Drain lines from cold top tables, bain-maries, ice cream scoop dipper wells, and food preparation sinks must have a minimum internal diameter of 1 inch (2.5 cm) and be cleanable in place with a long brush or easily removable for cleaning. 26. Drain lines with angles, corners, or sections longer than 3 feet (0.9 m) must be readily removable for cleaning. 27. Drain lines may be constructed of stainless steel or easily cleanable flexible or rigid materials. 28. Air breaks are acceptable for equipment drain lines. 29. Installed equipment drain lines, including condensate drain lines from refrigeration units, must minimize the piping distance from the drain line outlet to the deck scupper drain. 30. Drain lines should extend in a straight vertical line to a deck scupper drain whenever possible. 31. If a straight vertical line is not possible, the horizontal distance of the line should be kept to a minimum. 32. Horizontal drain lines under equipment mounted on legs must not extend for a distance greater than 12 inches (30.5 cm) and must be positioned at least 4 inches (10.2 cm) above the deck. 33. Electrical connections and control panels on all equipment and bulkheads must be watertight and drip-proof, meeting the International Electrical Code. 34. Electrical wiring from permanently installed equipment must be encased in stainless steel. 35. Ozone or ultraviolet equipment must not be installed in provisions rooms or food preparation areas unless constructed of non-corroding stainless steel with fasteners meeting Section VI requirements. 36. Bulkhead-mounted equipment installations, such as phones, speakers, and cameras, must be sealed tightly with the bulkhead panels and not placed in areas exposed to moisture, food splash, or grease. 37. Areas where electrical lines, steam, or water pipelines penetrate panels or tiles of the deck, bulkhead, or deckhead must be tightly sealed. 38. Openings between electrical lines, steam or water pipelines, and the surrounding conduit or pipelines must also be sealed. 39. Steam and water pipelines to kettles and boilers must be encased in stainless steel cabinets or positioned behind bulkhead panels, with minimal exposed pipeline acceptable. 40. Hood systems must be installed over ware washing equipment, including three-compartment sinks in pot wash areas, to capture excess steam and vapors. 41. Ware washing machines with direct duct exhaust must be directly connected to the hood exhaust trunk. 42. Exhaust hoods over ware washing equipment or three-compartment sinks must have a minimum six-inch overhang from the edge of the equipment to capture excess steam and vapors. 43. Ware washing machines with direct duct exhaust to the ventilation system must have a clean-out port in each duct, located between the top of the machine and the hood system or deckhead. 44. Flat condensate drip pans in ducts from ware washing machines must be removable for cleaning. 45. Hood systems must be installed above cooking equipment to adequately remove excess steam and grease-laden vapors. 46. Excess heat and steam from bain-maries or steam tables must be controlled by hood systems or dedicated local ventilation extraction. 47. Exhaust vents must be appropriately sized and located to capture heat and steam effectively. 48. Filters used in ventilation systems must be easily removable. 49. Vents and ductwork must be accessible for cleaning, and hood washing systems are recommended for removing grease generated from cooking equipment. 50. Hood systems must be constructed using stainless steel with coved corners providing at least a 3/8 inch (9.5 mm) radius. 51. Continuous welds or profile strips must be used on adjoining pieces of stainless steel in hood systems. 52. Drainage systems are not required for manually applied cleaning solutions or grease from hood assemblies but are required for hood assemblies utilizing automatic wash-down systems. 53. Ventilation systems must comply with manufacturers' recommendations. 54. Bulkheads and deckheads in walk-in refrigerators and freezers must use tight-fitting stainless steel panels with seams less than 1/32 inch (0.8 mm). 55. Stainless steel panels are preferable for dry storage areas, while painted steel may be used for provisions passageways and dry stores areas.
